descriptor: ASX gold producer (Duketon, Tropicana, McPhillamys) · Jun FY · reported in AUD

charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income

sections.title: Gold Production & Costs
sections.subtitle: Ounces produced/sold, all-in sustaining cost and the achieved gold price -- the operating drivers behind Revenue and EBITDA above

charts.title: AISC vs Gold Price Achieved
charts.annotation: The spread between the two lines is the operating margin per ounce -- Regis's core unit economics.

charts.title: Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Owner FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown, is the DCF's series after SBC, interest income and lease principal. Net income in FY2021 is depressed by the A$885m Tropicana acquisition cost; FY2023 carries a A$39m stamp duty charge on the Tropicana stake; FY2024 carries a A$98m one-off cost to buy out the legacy hedge book -- none are ongoing.

charts.title: Operating Cash Flow & CapEx
charts.annotation: FY2021 CapEx/cash flow includes the A$885m cash cost of acquiring the 30% Tropicana stake -- a one-off, not sustaining capital.

goldVolume.title: Gold produced vs gold sold
goldVolume.content:
Gold produced is ounces mined and poured in the period; gold sold is ounces actually shipped and invoiced, which can lead or lag production as doré/bullion inventory builds or draws down.

For Regis Resources: production is the sum of Duketon (McPhillamys is pre-production) plus its 30% share of Tropicana since the FY2021 acquisition; a sustained gap between produced and sold ounces flags inventory timing rather than an operating problem.

What to watch:

  • Sold consistently tracking produced over a full year
  • Production trend against reserve/mine-life guidance

aiscPrice.title: AISC vs gold price achieved
aiscPrice.content:
All-in sustaining cost (AISC) is the fully loaded cash cost per ounce, including sustaining capital; gold price achieved is the average realised A$/oz across spot sales and any hedging.

For Regis Resources: the company ran a legacy hedge book that capped realised prices below spot for years until it was bought out in FY2024 (a ~A$98m one-off cost); post-buyout, achieved price tracks the spot gold price much more closely.

What to watch:

  • AISC inflation eroding the per-ounce margin even as spot gold rises
  • Achieved price versus spot gold price (hedge drag pre-FY2024)

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Regis Resources Limited: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Regis Resources Limited: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Regis Resources Limited: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Regis Resources Limited: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Regis Resources Limited: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Regis Resources Limited: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Regis Resources Limited: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Regis Resources Limited: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Regis Resources Limited: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Regis Resources Limited: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
